subject: Next steps + model fit evals - Redwood & PayGrid
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@paygrid.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps + model fit evals - Redwood & PayGrid

Hey Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for the time today - good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the model fit evaluation moving:

1) Recap from our call
- Primary objective: reduce customer support completion time by surfacing actionable answers from transaction-level logs and routing intents to the right team.
- Tech constraints: PII must not leave PayGrid; evaluation needs to run on a redacted sample or in your VPC.
- Success criteria: parity with your current proprietary baseline on intent accuracy, and no significant regressions on hallucination on the critical 200-case prompt set.

2) What Redwood will deliver (initial pass)
- Recommended model candidates: Open models (Llama 3 13B chat, OpenLlama 30B quantized) and Redwood-optimized baseline (rw-infer-13b-pro).
- We will run a parity eval using the prompt set you shared and an internal anonymized subset we use for safety checks.
- Deliverables: prompt set (attached), initial benchmark CSV, and a mutual action plan (attached).

3) Ask from PayGrid
- Confirm whether you can run evals in your VPC or if we should use a redacted sample in our sandbox.
- Provide any additional high-priority prompts beyond the attached prompt set (paygrid_prompt_set_v1.json).

Proposed timeline
- Week 0 (this week): agree on dataset and access model.
- Week 1: Redwood runs initial benchmarks and shares results.
- Week 2: joint review and threshold tuning.

Acceptance thresholds we typically use for parity discussions: within 2% absolute on intent accuracy and no increase in hallucination FPR above 1.5x baseline. Those are starting points; we can adjust based on your risk tolerance.

Attachments: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.json, mutual_action_plan.xlsx (stubbed).

I'll schedule a 30-min sync next Tue; if you prefer an earlier slot ping me and I'll adjust.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
From: Samir Patel <samir@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@paygrid.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps + model fit evals - Redwood & PayGrid

Lauren - thanks for the clear recap. A few quick Qs before we lock the timeline:

- On the "rw-infer-13b-pro": can you share a short description of what that baseline represents (training data differences / any safety filters)?
- On thresholds: the 2% intent accuracy delta seems reasonable but our legal/compliance team will want to sign off on the hallucination tolerance. Can you share how you measure hallucination FPR?
- For VPC vs sandbox: we prefer VPC run if possible. We can get a redacted subset ready but will need a short onboarding doc for your team to access the eval harness.

Also looping Elena - she owns integrations and will validate the data export.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of ML Platform | PayGrid
samir@paygrid.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@paygrid.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps + model fit evals - Redwood & PayGrid

Samir - great questions, answers below and attaching the initial benchmark CSV (stub) with our measurement definitions.

Short answers:
- rw-infer-13b-pro: Redwood-optimized 13B chat variant with inference-time safety filters and KV cache optimizations; trained / finetuned on a mix of public data + synthetic dialogue for instruction-following. I can share a short tech note if you want details.

- Hallucination FPR: we measure hallucination by taking a labelled subset of prompts where ground-truth is known (the 200-case critical set) and count false positive assertions that are confidently stated by the model but unsupported by context. FPR = false positives / total negatives in the labeled set. We include confidence thresholding; the initial CSV shows sample numbers.

Recommended candidate list for the parity eval (first pass):
- Open option A: Llama 3 13B-chat (float16) - good latency, strong instruction following.
- Open option B: OpenLlama 30B quantized (int8/mmapped) - better on recall tasks, slightly higher latency.
- Redwood baseline: rw-infer-13b-pro (our tuned baseline).

Benchmark links and artifacts
- Initial benchmarks (attached): redwood_initial_benchmark.csv (stub) - includes intent accuracy, top-1 routing accuracy, hallucination FPR, and 95th latency percentiles.
- Prompt set: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.json (attached).
- Shared Drive with evaluation harness and expected data formatting: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-paygrid-evals

Proposed evaluation approach
- Run candidate models against the same redacted prompt set with identical temperature/decoding settings.
- Primary metric: intent accuracy (macro) and hallucination FPR on the critical 200-case set.
- Secondary metrics: latency p95 and token cost.

If VPC evaluation is the preference, Marissa (cc) can take the lead on onboarding and supply the evaluation container we use for private runs. Otherwise we can operate on a redacted sample in our sandbox for the initial pass.

Next step: can you confirm the dataset access method and whether legal needs any additional artifacts up front? If you confirm VPC, Marissa will send the onboarding doc and an MNP (minimal network policy) template.

Thanks,
Lauren
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@paygrid.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@paygrid.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps + model fit evals - Redwood & PayGrid

Samir / Elena - Marissa here, looping in on the technical onboarding and thresholds. Quick notes:

- On onboarding: we prefer VPC private-run for production-sensitive data. I'll send the onboarding doc and a minimal container that runs the eval harness. ETA for our onboarding doc: EOD today.

- Acceptance thresholds (recommended starting points):
  * Intent accuracy: parity within 2% absolute (model vs your proprietary baseline)
  * Hallucination FPR: no more than 1.5x current baseline on the critical 200-case set (we'll provide per-prompt breakdowns)
  * Latency: p95 at or below 1.25x of baseline for addressable production routes

- If PayGrid needs a stricter hallucination constraint for legal sign-off, we can add a post-processing verifier step as an optional mitigation; we can scope that after the initial eval.

Proposed mutual action plan milestones (see attached MAP):
- Day 0: Agree dataset & access method
- Day 3: Redwood runs initial VPC onboarding & smoke tests
- Day 7: Initial parity pass and CSV share
- Day 14: Joint review and decision on next phase (pilot / rollout)

I'll follow up with the onboarding doc and the MNP template. Looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
